statement: Solve $3\sin\theta+4\cos\theta=2$ for $0\le\theta<2\pi$, giving your answers exactly in terms of inverse trigonometric functions.
solution: From the R-form, $3\sin\theta+4\cos\theta=5\sin(\theta+\alpha)$ where $\cos\alpha=3/5,\sin\alpha=4/5$ and $\alpha=\arctan(4/3)$. So $5\sin(\theta+\alpha)=2\Rightarrow \sin(\theta+\alpha)=\tfrac25$. Let $\beta=\arcsin(2/5)$. Then $\theta+\alpha=\beta$ or $\pi-\beta$ (mod $2\pi$). Thus $\theta=\beta-\alpha$ or $\pi-\beta-\alpha$ within $[0,2\pi)$, i.e. $\theta=\arcsin(2/5)-\arctan(4/3)$ and $\theta=\pi-\arcsin(2/5)-\arctan(4/3)$ (adjusted into range).
